MINUTES OF THE MORNING SESSION
FRIDAY, JUNE 19. 1942
Adams Memorial Theatre, Williams College
Williamstown. Massachusetts
BEFORE
the formal opening of the 109th annual Convention of the
Psi Upsilon Fraternity, Professor Richard A. Newhall. Acting Presi
dent of Williams College, was presented by Brother Gordon T. Getsinger,
Delta Delta '43. Professor Newhall officially welcomed the delegates of
the Convention to Williamstown.
After Professor Newhall had withdrawn, the Convention was called
to order at 9 :20 A.M. at the Adams Memorial Theatre, Williams College,
Williamstown, Massachusetts, by Scott Turner, Phi '02, President of the
Executive Council, who appointed the following temporary officers :
Temporary President�
Gordon T. Getsinger, Delta Delta '43
Temporary Recorder�
John F. Morgan, Delta Delta '43
Brother Getsinger welcomed the Convention delegates on behalf of the
Delta Delta and its alumni, and he then appointed the following committees,
by customary rotation :
On Credentials:
Daniel H. Huyett, III, Phi '42, Chairman
George Krakowka, Omega '42
John F. Harper. Chi '43
On Permanent Organ/isotion:
Alan Miller, Beta Beta '42, Chairman
Ward A. Detwiler, II, Eta '42
Robert C. Beck, Tau '43
Motion was duly made, seconded, and passed, that the Convention take
a recess to enable the committees to prepare their reports.
At the end of the recess, Temporary President Gordon T. Getsinger,
Delta Delta '43, called the Convention to order.
The Committee on Credentials reported that the following delegates
had presented their credentials which were in order :

Scott Turner, Phi '02

On motion duly made, seconded, and passed, this report was accepted.
The Committee on Permanent Organization presented its report, making
the following nominations for officers of this Convention :
President Scott Turner, Phi '02
1st Vice-President Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21
2nd Vice-President John B. Clapp, Delta Delta '18
3rd Vice-President Jerome W. Brush, Jr., Delta Delta '39
4th Vice-President Charles H. Toll, Psi '04
5th Vice-President C. T. S. Keep, Delta Delta '28
6th Vice-President A. Northey Jones, Beta Beta '17
Recorder John F. Morgan. Delta Delta '43
Assistant Recorder William G. Morrisey, III. Delta Delta '43
Assistant Recorder George G. Bass. Jr.. Delta Delta '44
On motion duly made, seconded, and passed, this report was unani
mously accepted, and the Temporary Recorder was instructed to cast one
ballot for the election of the Permanent Officers nominated.
President Turner then took the Chair, and read a letter from Brother
Stephen G. Kent, Delta Delta '11. The Convention Rules formerly used
were read by the Recorder ; a motion made, seconded, and passed that the
rules as read govern this Convention.
President Turner introduced to the undergraduate delegates the follow
ing alumni present at the meeting: Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21; John B.
Clapp, Delta Delta '18; A. Northey Jones, Beta Beta '17; Herbert J. Flagg,
Theta Theta '12; Oliver B. Merrill, Jr., Gamma '25; C. Terry S. Keep,
Delta Delta '28; Stowell C. Stebbins. Phi '12; Harry W. Bosworth. Psi
'05 ; Samuel W. Wolcott. Delta Delta '18.

B. T. Burton, Chi '21
The Annual Communication of the Executive Council was read by
Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21. Vice-President of the Executive Council.
On motion duly made, seconded, and passed, this Communication was
accepted, and referred to the Committee on Annual Communications.
Allen Northey Jones, Beta Beta '17, Treasurer of the Executive Coun
cil, read the annual Treasurer's Report, copies of which were passed to
the delegates. After discussion, and on motion duly made, seconded, and
passed, the Treasurer's Report was accepted and referred to the Com
mittee on Annual Communications.
President Turner distributed to the delegates copies of the Vital
Statistics of the Psi Upsilon Chapters.
Oral reports were given by the delegates from the following Chapters.
each report being followed by discussion:
Page Five

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
Gamma Psi Iota
Zeta Phi
Motion was duly made, seconded, and passed, to refer the invitation
tendered by the Psi Chapter for the 1943 National Convention to the Com
mittee on Unfinished Business.
Herbert J. Flagg, Theta Theta '12, Chairman of the Committee on Annual
Communications, presented the report of the Committee. The Committee
congratulated the Executive Council and the Treasurer on the excellently
prepared reports submitted to the Convention. The Convention ordered
them to be included in the Convention Records.
The petition of the Hesperian Society of Michigan State College for
admission into the Psi Upsilon Fraternity was referred to the Committee
on New Business, and an interim report was requested by President Turner
for the afternoon meeting.
Stowell C. Stebbins, Phi '12, spoke on behalf of the Hesperian Society
and asked the delegates to consider its petition most carefully.
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, the Convention adjourned
until 2:00 P.M., Friday, June 19, 1942.
MINUTES OF THE AFTERNOON SESSION
FRIDAY, JUNE 19, 1942
Adams Memorial Theatre, Williams College
Williamstown, Massachusetts
The meeting was called to order by President Turner at 2:15 P.M.
The minutes of the morning session were read, and, after correction,
on motion duly made, seconded, and passed, were approved.
The Committee on Credentials received from the following delegates
their credentials, which were in order:
Mu�Herbert J. Parker. Jr., '42
Sigma�Edwin B. Laughlin, '43
Credentials of Walter T. Collins, Iota '03, Herbert J. Flagg, Theta
Theta '12, and Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21. members of the Executive
Council, were also presented.
President Turner read the interim report presented by Charles B.
Tennant, Psi '43, Chairman of the Committee on New Business. It recom
mended that the Convention resolve itself into a Committee of the Whole,
to listen to and discuss the petition of the Hesperian Society of Michigan
State College for a charter from Psi Upsilon. The Committee further
recommended that the Convention then take a recess and invite the repre
sentatives of the petitioners to appear before it, after which the Convention
should re-convene and decide whether the Hesperian petition should or
should not be referred to the Chapters for appropriate action.
Page Six

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
After discussion, and on motion duly made, seconded, and passed, the
Committee's report was accepted. The Convention resolved itself into a
Committee of the Whole at 2:25 P.M., and so continued until 3:00 P.M.
President Turner stepped down from the Chair and asked Brother Tennant
to lead discussion of the qualifications of the Hesperian Society.
At the expiration of the time allotted to the Committee of the Whole,
the Convention was again in session, and a motion was duly made, seconded,
and passed that the Convention take a recess to enable the representatives
of the Hesperian Society to appear before the Convention. After their oral
support of the petition had been presented, the guests left the hall, and
President Turner again called the Convention to order.
President Turner then read the article of the Constitution relating to
the adoption of a new Chapter into the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.
A motion was duly made, seconded, and unanimously passed to refer
the petition of the Hesperian Society to each of the Chapters, where a
favorable vote by two-thirds of the members of each Chapter must be
cast if the Hesperian Society is to secure a Charter.
Oral reports on the state of their Chapters were given by the delegates
from the following Chapters:
Omega Pi Chi Xi
President Turner introduced to the undergraduate delegates the fol
lowing alumni present at the meeting: William L. Tierney, Jr., Delta
Delta '28 ; Dr. Charles S. F. Lincoln, Kappa '91 ; Hamilton Holt, Beta '94 ;
Reinald Werrenrath, Delta '05 ; Walter T. Collins, Iota '03.
On motion, duly made, seconded, and passed, the Convention adjourned
until 9:00 A.M., Saturday, June 20, 1942.
MINUTES OF THE MORNING SESSION
SATURDAY. JUNE 20. 1942
Adams Memorial Theatre. Williams College
Williamstown, Massachusetts
The Convention was called to order by President Turner at 9 :10 A.M.
The minutes of the previous afternoon session were read and, on motion
duly made, seconded, and passed, were approved.
Oral Reports of the following Chapters were made by the delegates
present :
Kappa Xi Eta Tau
The Convention adjourned for a ten-minute recess to enable the various
standing committees to prepare their reports. At the end of the recess.
President Turner again called the Convention to order.
The Chairman of the Committee on Credentials presented a report on

the number of delegates present; those delegates who lacked credentials
were recommended by the Committee for seats at the Convention. On
motion duly made, seconded, and passed, this recommendation was adopted.

Herbert Parker, Jr., Mu '42, Chairman, presented the report of the
Committee to Nominate Members of the Executive Council. The following
Brothers were nominated for membership on the Executive Council for the
usual term of five years :
Samuel L. Rosenberry, Rho '23
Herbert J. Flagg, Theta Theta '12
Roswell G. Flam, Epsilon '14
Motion was duly made, seconded, and passed that the report be adopted
and that the Recorder be instructed to cast a single ballot electing each
of the Brothers nominated to the Executive Council for the usual term of
five years.
The report of the Committee on Unfinished Business was read by H.
Bradley Benedict, Gamma '43, recommending the adoption of the following
resolutions :
1. Resolved: That each of the Chapters appoint two officers,,
one undergraduate and one alumnus, whose duty it will be to keep
the Chapter histories up-to-date, subsequent to their publication in
the Annals of Psi Upsilon ; and that the names of these officers be
reported to the Executive Council.
2. Resolved: That General Resolution No. 6, as adopted by
the 1937 Convention, applying to the importance of scholastic stand
ing, be earnestly adhered to by the various Chapters, and that a copy
of this resolution be forwarded by the Executive Council each Sep
tember to every Chapter.
Page Eight

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
3. Resolved: That the Convention accept with thanks the in
vitation of the Psi Chapter to hold the 1943 Convention with that
Chapter.
Upon motion, duly made, seconded, and passed, this report was accepted.
President Turner then called for further Chapter reports, which were
given by the delegates from the following Chapters :
Mu Rho Omicron
On motion duly made, seconded, and passed, it was voted to adjourn
the Convention until Saturday, June 20, at 2:00 P.M.
MINUTES OF THE AFTERNOON SESSION
SATURDAY, JUNE 20, 1942
Adams Memorial Theatre. Williams College
Williamstown, Massachusetts
The Convention was called to order by President Turner at 2:00 P.M.
The minutes of the previous morning session were read and, on motion
duly made, seconded, and passed, were approved.
President Turner introduced Peter- A. GaBauer. Pi '25, who spoke to
the Convention in his capacity of Archivist.
John B. Clapp, Delta Delta '18, President of the Psi Upsilon Alumni
of Boston, announced the establishment of a scholarship fund by that group
to be awarded periodically to an undergraduate of some New England
Chapter of Psi Upsilon. He said that financial need and worth to the
college would determine the award, and announced that it was to be made
this year to Morris S. Dampier, Zeta '43.
Oral reports of the following Chapters were made by the delegates
present :
Theta Beta Beta
Delta Omicron
Sigma Delta Delta
Upsilon
'
Theta Theta
President Turner read a report published by the National Interfrater
nity Conference, which outlined the antagonism directed against fraternities
from Washington during the last war and which cautioned fraternities to
conduct themselves now so that no such attack could be sustained.
The report of the Committee on New Business was read by Charles
B. Tennant, Psi '43, Chairman. It recommended the adoption of the fol-
'
lowing resolutions :
1. Resolved: That the Recorder be directed to write an expres
sion of gratitude to Professor Richard A. Newhall, Acting President
Page Nine

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
of Williams College, for his welcome to the Convention on behalf of
�
the College.
2. Resolved: That this Convention hereby express to Williams
College appreciation for its cordial hospitality and generous extension
of campus facilities to the delegates and alumni.
3. Resolved: That the delegates and members, assembled in
the 109th year of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, extend their gratitude
to the Delta Delta Chapter, its undergraduates and alumni, for the
cordial reception extended to those attending the Convention.
4. Resolved: That the Convention is grateful to the members
of the Executive Council, and the officers of the Council, for their
untiring efforts on behalf of the Chapters and the Fraternity as a
whole.
5. Resolved: That the Convention hereby records its appre
ciation of the unselfish and effective efforts of the Board of Gov
ernors of the Alumni Association and its officers.
6. Resolved: That the delegates to this Convention convey to
the Council's Advisory Committee on The Diamond, and to the
members of the Editorial Staff, their thanks and their appreciation
for the excellent work done during the year.
7. Resolved: That the Recorder be directed to send telegrams
of greeting from the Convention to each of the Past Presidents of
the Executive Council: Earl D. Babst. Iota 1893; Edward L.
Stevens, Chi 1899; Archibald Douglas, Lambda 1894.
8. Resolved: That the delegates to this Convention express to
Brother Scott Turner, Phi 1902. President of the Executive Council
of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity and President of this Convention.
their appreciation for his work in presiding over all the sessions of
this Convention and for the able manner in which he has conducted
the meetings.
9. Resolved: That the delegates to this Convention express
their gratitude to all the Officers of this Convention and to the
Committees reporting to the Convention, for the efficient manner in
which they have handled the work allotted to them.
10. Resolved: That the Recorder send a telegram to Stephen
G. Kent, Delta Delta 1911. Secretary of the Executive Council, ex
pressing sympathy for his recent bereavement and regret at his in
ability to attend the Convention.
11. Resolved: That in all official records and literature of the
Page Ten

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
Fraternity, each Brother be designated by the name or symbol of the
Chapter which initiated him only and not by any combination of,
or use of more than one Chapter-name or symbol.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, the report of the Com
mittee on New Business was accepted and each of the recommended reso
lutions, other than Resolution No. 11. was unanimously adopted.
Upon motion duly made, seconded, and passed, Resolution No. 11 was
amended to read as follows :
11. Resolved: That in all records and literature of the Frater
nity, each Brother be designated by the name or symbol of the
Chapter which initiated him only, and npt by any combination of.
or use of more than one. Chapter-name or symbol.
As so amended, the resolution was unanimously adopted.
Motion was duly made, seconded, and passed that a tabulated list of
the names of members attending the Convention should be added to the
formal records of the Convention.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted that the
Convention be adjourned sine die.
There being no further business. President Scott Turner, Phi '02,
declared the Convention adjourned, sine die, at 4:40 P.M.
Respectfully submitted,
John F. Morgan,
Delta Delta '43, Recorder
RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED
General Resolutions
General Resolution No. 1. Resolved: That the petition of the Hes
perian Society be referred to each of the Chapters, where a favorable vote
by two-thirds of the members of each Chapter must be cast if the Hesperian
Society is to secure a Charter.
General Resolution No. 2. Resolved: That the Recorder be instructed
to cast a single ballot electing each of the following brothers:
Samuel L. Rosenberry, Rho '23
Herbert J. Flagg. Theta Theta '12
Roswell G. Ham. Epsilon '14
to the Executive Council for the usual term of five years.
General Resolution No. 3. Resolved: That each of the Chapters ap
point two officers, one undergraduate and one alumnus, whose duty it will

Appendix A
THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION
OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL
TO THE
1942 CONVENTION OF PSI UPSILON
HELD UNDER THE AUSPICES OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL AND THE DELTA DELTA CHAPTER
Williamstown. Massachusetts
June 19 and 20. 1942
The Executive Council extends cordial welcome and fraternal greeting
to the delegates of our twenty-seven Chapters to this Convention, held in
the one hundred and ninth year of our Fraternity.
The Fraternity is deeply grateful to Williams College, to its President.
Dr. James Phinney Baxter. 3rd. and to its Board of Trustees, for their
hospitality in making the buildings and facilities of the College available
to our delegates.
We wish to express our warm appreciation of the thoughtfulness and
generosity of the undergraduates, alumni, and Convention Committee, of
the Delta Delta. The success of the Convention will be largely owing to
the careful arrangements made by them.
Chapter Visits:
Since our last Convention, the following five official visits to Chapters
have been made : To the Sigma. A. Northey Jones ; the Zeta. Harold L.
Berry; the Lambda, Benjamin T. Burton; the Eta, Herbert J. Flagg; and
to the Epsilon, Alfred H. Morton. In addition, pursuant to General Reso
lution No. 3 of the Convention of 1939, under appointment by the Executive
Council, Brothers R. Bourke Corcoran and Gordon B. McLaren, made visits
to the Omega and Zeta Zeta Chapters respectively.
The Condition of the Fraternity :
Psi Upsilon Chapters are maintaining a fair state of health, despite
world conditions. A study of the Table of Vital Statistics shows an active
membership of 850 on March 1, 1942. as against 895 the previous year.
Those who graduated from college in 1941 numbered 194. 41 less than in
1940. Those leaving college without graduating rose from 179 to 271 in
tbe same period; of this number. 123 entered the military services.
Page Seventeen

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
It cannot be expected that this comparatively favorable state will con
tinue. The war will decrease enrollment in our chapters, and in the colleges
where we have chapters. Increasing numbers of undergraduates will be
absorbed in the Army and Navy. Per capita costs of operation of our
houses will rise. Financial difficulties may multiply, and undergraduates
and alumni must be alert to the dangers which may threaten.
Psi Upsilon already has its honor roll of those who have given their
lives in this war. Up to the present time, we have received six notices;
these were regarding Brothers Carl A. Bergsten, Pi '39 ; Gilbert Clarence
Bills, Delta Delta-Omega '42 ; Richard Edward Jacques, Omega '40 ; Gordon
Campbell O'Neill, Epsilon Phi '41; Carl Andrew Weiant. Jr.. Iota '37;
and Clarence Allen Wright. Omega '37. Doubtless there are other names
which have not yet been reported to us.
The Annals of Psi Upsilon :
The past year has been marked by the publication and distribution of
more than three thousand copies of The Annals of Psi Upsilon, the prepa
ration of which was reported to the 1941 Convention. As the work of
gathering material for the volume progressed, plans for its scope were
enlarged; the finished work is unquestionably the most distinguished and
comprehensive volume ever issued by an American college fraternity.
The Archives :
Farther improvement in the Archives has been made during the year,
along the lines first reported in our annual communication two years ago,
at which time the records of the Fraternity were removed from limbo in
a warehouse and installed in adequate and appropriate quarters connected
with our business office. In the preparation of The Annals, much valuable
material was unearthed in various places, and brought together here for
safe keeping. Recently, the Archives Room was enlarged and re-arranged
for the more efficient care of our growing collection of valuable memora
bilia. We suggest that Brothers coming to the Metropolitan area make it
a point to visit Headquarters, sign the Visitor's Book, and inspect the
Archives of the Fraternity.
The Diamond:
Under the editorship of Brother Jerome W. Brush, Jr., Delta Delta '39,
the Diamond has had a successful year, and has maintained its standing as
an excellent fraternity magazine. Brother Fales resigned as chairman of
the Advisory Committee, and Brother Alfred H. Morton was appointed
to serve for the balance of the year.
Scholarship :
The scholarship of the various chapters has shown no marked improvePage Eighteen

PSI UPSI LON FRATERNITY
ment over the almost uniformly unsatisfactory records of previous years.
In the hope of helping to correct this condition, the Executive Council's
Scholarship Committee, headed by Brother Edward T. Richards, and in
cluding Brothers Woolman and Flagg, prepared a report which contained
a number of practical suggestions ; this was sent to the chapters and was
published in the March issue of the Diamond. Each chapter, whose
scholarship record is low. should give earnest consideration to this report.
and should endeavor to make use of the recommendations best adapted to
its particular needs.
Alumni Association of Psi Upsilon :
The officers and Board of Governors of the Alumni Association have
continued to give devoted service to the Fraternity during the past year.
Life members of the Association now number well over two hundred. With
the Lambda Alumni Association, the Psi Upsilon Alumni Association spon
sored a dinner in New York City on May 1. 1942, which combined the
function of an annual get-together for alumni in the Metropolitan area with
that of a celebration of the centennial of the Lambda Chapter.
Petitions :
The Executive Council received a petition from the Hesperian Society
at Michigan State College; under the provisions of a part of Article II.
Section 6. of the Constitution, the Council investigated this application, and,
as required, takes this opportunity to transmit it to the Convention, with
the suggestion that it be given serious and sympathetic consideration.
The Executive Council:
The Executive Council has performed its allotted functions during the
year. It held six meetings, on October 7th and November Sth, 1941, and
January 5th, March 9th, May 4th, and June 8th, of this year, at each of
which attendance was excellent. Many problems have been given full and
timely consideration and discussion, often with alumni and undergraduates
present from various chapters. At one of its meetings, the members of the
Board of Governors of the Alumni Association attended by special invita
tion, and, at another meeting, the members of the Advisory Committee on
the Diamond were guests. Invitations to attend each meeting were mailed
to each former member of Council living near New York City. The
Council still favors the plan adopted three years ago of having interested
alumni sponsor the visits of heads of the Chapter houses to Council meet
ings. It is urged that the presidents of the Chapter Alumni Associations
each try to attend at least one meeting of the Executive Council during
the year. Visiting alumni are made welcome at meetings.
With this Convention, expire the terms of Brothers Francis N. Bangs.

Roswell Gray Ham, and Herbert Judson Flagg. It is, therefore, the duty
of the Convention to elect three brothers to the Executive Council, each
of whom will serve for the regular term of five years.
1943 Convention :
The Executive Council recognizes the desirability of preserving the
continuity of its annual conventions ; these thoroughly representative assem
blies, among the oldest and most continuous deliberative bodies in this
country, have become traditional with us. Therefore it is believed that
we should continue to hold these conventions, if need be on a reduced
scale both as to time and money involved, until such time as it may become
practically impossible to do so.
The Psi Chapter has recently expressed its desire to act as host to the
1943 Convention. The year 1943 will mark its centennial, as well as that
of two other Chapters, the Kappa and the Xi. The Executive Council
greatly appreciated the spirit shown by the Psi Chapter in extending this
invitation, and offers it for your prompt and sympathetic consideration.
Membership in National Interfraternity Conference:
Recognizing the wisdom of presenting a united front to the subversive
forces bent on the elimination of the institution of the college fraternity
from scholastic life in this country, the Executive Council retains member
ship for the Fraternity in the Conference. Of the sixty eligible fraternities,
all are now members, thus focusing in one representative organization the
care for the needs and interests of the 2500 chapters and one million mem
bers of these sixty Greek-letter organizations. Full recognition has been
accorded us in the inner councils of Conference, and at the present time
the President of the Executive Council of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
Brother Scott Turner, Phi 1902, is a member of the Executive Committee
of National Interfraternity Conference, Chairman of its important Com
mittee on Policy, and Chairman of its special committee dealing with
financial problems. Thus we find ourselves closely in touch with the new
situations constantly arising between the fraternities, the colleges, and the
public, and we have been enabled to make provision to meet such situations
as appeared to require attention.
General :
All the English-speaking part of this continent, from which we draw
our members, is at war. Putting aside all questions of how this came to
pass, what political and economic factors were involved, what leadership
is available to us, and how great the burden may become, the fact remains
that the only way out is to win the war. That is the proposition with
which all are faced. The active work of winning will fall largely on the

youngsters'
�
such men as are represented by the delegates assembled at this
Convention. When this war is won, you too will have the life-long burden
of paying for it. Therefore, there is every reason why each of you should
give thought and attention to how you may best conduct yourselves to
discharge your obligations to family, associate, fellow-citizen, to your frater
nity, and to your country.
It should be obvious that certain things are fundamentally important
in preparing yourselves for the struggle which you now face. It would be
unthinkable that college or fraternity life should be the same as before
the war. At the outset, it would be wise to decide to stay where you are
and finish your course, unless called for military service ; but strive to put
more into, and get more out of, your college work. Perhaps you can get
some pre-service training there. Cut down your leisure time; try to work
more effectively so that you get more done each day and thus develop
faster. Endeavor to put yourself in fine physical and mental condition, and
keep that way. Eliminate waste of time, money, thought, and energy. Go
at this big task seriously. Tighten your belts. Cultivate Spartan charac
teristics. Make every hour count. Get ready for the job in hand; it will
need all you can give it.
As loyal fraternity men, if you handle yourselves properly, you can
make an opportunity now to show the world that the college fraternity
may be a great influence for good in time of crisis. More and more people
seem to doubt that the fraternity system has justified its existence during
the past twenty-five years. It is recognized that a great change in the
status of fraternities began just after the World War. We of Psi Upsilon
have never admitted that our usefulness has lessened, or that our vision
has been impaired, during our long period of existence. Now we have a
good chance to prove it. Let Psi Upsilon lead in this, as it has in so many
other ways. Put your house in order. Regulate your finances. Conserve
your time. Study hard. Eliminate frills. Develop your capacity for
leadership. Do well the task before you. Get yourself ready to fight.
Make your chapter-house the center of sober plan and endeavor ; let' it show
leadership in cooperating with college and local authorities; emphasize the
spiritual values which are part of our inheritance; make it known that Psi
Upsilon intends to make the enemies of its country feel its might.
Respectfully submitted.
The Committee of the Executive Council of Psi Upsilon
ON the Annual Communication to the 1942 Convention.
Scott Turner, Phi '02
Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21
Stephen G. Kent, Delta Delta '11

Appendix B
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL OF PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
Report of the Treasurer
1942
There is presented herewith a statement of the net worth of the various
funds of the Fraternity held by the Executive Council as of April 30, 1942,
a summary of income and expenses of the various funds for the year ended
April 30, 1942, and certain comparative figures for the year ended April 30,
1941. A list of investments held in the General Fund, the Bridgman Fund
and the Diamond Life Subscription Fund, showing the cost and market
value, is also presented.
It is to be noted that a new fund has been created this past fiscal year,
namely the Archives Fund. Brother Earl D. Babst requested that this
fund be created, and gave 100 copies of the Annals of Psi Upsilon to
establish it. Of these 100 copies SO have been sold, so that there is now
$175 of cash in the fund and 50 copies of the Annals. No disbursements
have been made from this fund, as all Archives expenses have been met
either from donations or from the General Fund of the Fraternity.
The cash position of the Fraternity has been improved since April 30th
by the collection of chapter taxes which were then unpaid. All chapters
have paid all their chapter taxes and Diamond life subscriptions, with the
exception of the Zeta Zeta which owes $210 for Diamond life subscriptions.
Accounts payable (net) amounting to $585.74 shown in the Convention Fund
column were incurred because of the allowance of $500 to the entertaining
chapter and $212.49 toward the expenses of far western convention delegates.
The $500 allowance to the entertaining chapter has been paid to the Delta
Delta since April 30th.
The situation with respect to our investments is bad. We have an un
realized loss on our securities based on April 30th market values of
almost $14,000. Securities costing $2,300.97 were sold during the year for
$643.49, resulting in a loss of $1,657.48. If our investments were carried
in the statement at market value instead of cost, the aggregate net worth
of the funds of the Fraternity would work out as $25,122.24.
Included among our liabilities is a reserve of $15,889.98 for Diamond
life subscriptions. This reserve has been accumulated in the past three
years. This policy of setting up Diamond life subscription moneys in a
reserve �
rather than of spending such subscription moneys to meet the
current running expenses of the Diamond is a vast improvement over the
preceding practice when no reserves were set up. The current Diamond
Fund showed a loss of $2,743.59 in 1942. which was met by a transfer of

$2,700 from the Bridgman Fund and by a reduction of $43.59 in the net
worth of the Diamond Fund. It is expected that the Diamond Life Sub
scription Fund will be gradually built up by payments of $15 for life
subscriptions, so that the publication costs of the Diamond can eventually
be met in a businesslike manner from annuity payrnents from the fund.
The income and expense accounts of the various funds are selfexplanatory.
The Secretary and Treasurer of the Fraternity are trustees of a fund
known as the Willard Fiske Fund, the assets of which are not shown in
the attached statement. This fund was started by a gift of $50 made in
1881 by Willard Fiske. who stipulated that the money be kept intact until
the fund reaches $1,000. when the income thereon becomes available for
the general purposes of the Fraternity. The fund now amounts to approxi
mately $675. which is deposited in two savings bank accounts.
Again the Treasurer wishes to reiterate that every effort is being made
to keep expenses, and consequently chapter taxes, at a minimum. Taxes
of $4 per man per year are low in comparison with taxes of other frater
nities.
The Treasurer takes this opportunity to thank the undergraduate Treas
urers of the Chapters for their cooperation.
Respectfully submitted,
Allen Northey Jones,
Treasurer.
